creator: Alexander Terp
description:
A greedy `**rest` arg kind collecting remaining tokens verbatim, flags included, plus argv-safe interpolation and child exit-code propagation. Designed already in `rest_args.md` and `makefile-use-case.md`.

Strong evidence - the heaviest-used script class is wrappers and none can use the args block for its main job. `cct` (1103 runs) opts out entirely with `@enable_args_block = 0` and hand-parses with `index_of` plus slice surgery across 25 lines. `dev` uses `get_args()[1:].join(" ")`, lossy on spaces and metacharacters, and that quoting bug comes from the author's own sketch at `makefile-use-case.md:109`.

Parked on size rather than merit: it's three features (collection, safe interpolation, exit-code propagation) and the middle one overlaps the shell-quoting decision in stretch. Worth being near the top of the next sprint.

The exit-code half is separable and smaller: an unhandled `$` failure exits 1 and never the child's code, because `core/shell.go:84-90` wraps it in a RadError carrying no code (`core/printer.go:197`). `cct:623-624` hand-rolls ``code = $`{cmd}` catch: exit(code)``; `dev` doesn't, so it reports 1 for every child failure.
title: Passthrough and rest args
